anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved: After still refreshes member state only in CP7 after the CP6 body edit succeeds, tests current heads against the saved pushed home E, fetches N9 before the `--is-ancestor` test, emits the exact `#14 skipped: head moved to 9999999, not in home` line, offers only #13 with the spec comment carrying bbbbbbb and the #12 URL, rechecks #13 before `gh pr close` without `--delete-branch`, and keeps both variants (contained advanced head eligible; no eligible members asks no question) with no home-history proof for member fixes. Two small spots where After is thinner than Before and could regress under further edits: Variant A drops the explicit note that the refresh still fetches `9999…` before the ancestry check, and the Variant A recheck is summarized as `each PR rechecked unchanged` rather than Before's `re-fetched immediately before its own gh pr close` with changed targets skipped and reported. Restoring those two sentences in Variant A would keep the eligibility and variants facts robust while retaining the aliases, checkpoint structure and menu-layout echo the Change introduced.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Nothing moved: both outputs refresh member state only after the successful push and body edit, fetch X before testing #14's ancestry against the saved pushed head E, print the exact `#14 skipped: head moved to 9999999, not in home` line, offer only #13 with the bbbbbbb comment and home URL under option 1, recheck #13 immediately before closing without branch deletion, and handle the contained-advanced and no-eligible variants without inferring member fixes from home's first-parent history. The expected fails→holds for eligibility is not borne out because Before already satisfied it on its own text, so this case cannot demonstrate the improvement. After is slightly tighter (explicitly stating '#13 ... contained in E' ties the ancestry check to the saved pushed SHA, and the contained-#14 variant explicitly says the comment uses the recorded handle ccccccc rather than the advanced head); keep that wording. One minor risk in After: the `<selected spec path>` slot with an explanatory sentence reads as a placeholder next to the literal URLs—if the judge later tightens the 'never as a placeholder' rule to spec paths, name the resolved path or state it must be the real selected path, as Before did with `<selected-spec-path>` paired with the seal flag.
